summary: Static analysis of .claude/hooks/protect_control_surface.sh: the protected-path regex is (^|[^A-Za-z0-9_./-])(preregistration/|...). The negated class excludes '/', so any ABSOLUTE path (/home/.../preregistration/G0.yaml, /home/.../.claude/settings.json, /home/.../docs/EVIDENCE_ARC.md) does not match. The Write and Edit tools only accept absolute paths, so layer 1 of C1/C2 does not intercept them; Bash with an absolute path also passes. Only relative paths in Bash are caught. Separately, the writes regex matches any '>' including '2>&1', so a read-only 'ls -la .claude/... 2>&1' was denied (over-broad, minor). NOT empirically demonstrated: doing so would mean writing into the control surface, which I will not do to prove a point.
hypothesis: Regex should be (^|/|[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]) or equivalent, and the supervisor should also pin preregistration/** and docs/EVIDENCE_*.md once a gate has results.
action_taken: Reported in the escalation with the exact one-line test the human can run.
